newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice posts strong gains on USDA data, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice posts strong gains on USDA data, weather.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended sharply higher on Friday, supported by a cut in USDA's long grain rice ending stocks projection and on rains in the southern U.S. which could slow plantings, traders said.
"The USDA reduced our ending carry of long grain," a trader said. "I construe these numbers as friendly."
USDA on Friday put long grain ending stocks at 9.1 million cwt, down from the previous estimate of 9.6 million cwt.
Weather continued to be a supportive factor. Heavy rains fell on Friday across portions of Texas and Arkansas, keeping farmers out of the fields, traders said.
"It's raining now in Arkansas and Texas," a floor source said. "They're in the prime planting window in Texas now and they're getting into it in Arkansas."
Rice ended 27-1/2 to eight cents per cwt higher with May up 27-1/2 at $11.64.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 700 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 194 lots.
